title: Debug Retrospective Orchestrator: Guided payload-to-runbook flow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a guided console experience that converts clusters of failed requests and retry traces into a structured retrospective and an editable runbook. The Orchestrator helps engineers triage recurring failures, surfaces probable root causes, maps relevant payload diffs and KV cache states, and offers scaffolded remediation steps that can be promoted to runbooks or playbooks for SRE/Oncall teams.
design_notes: Primary persona: backend/ML engineer on-call for inference services who needs to understand why a set of requests failed and produce a reliable mitigation (rollback, model variant, rate limit tweak, retry-policy change).

Mental model: users want to go from noisy incident signals -> deduplicated error clusters -> canonical error taxonomy node -> reproducible payload + variable diff -> remediation checklist. The UI must reduce cognitive friction while preserving raw payload access.

Trade-offs considered: (1) auto-classification vs manual tagging — we propose a hybrid workflow where ML-assisted taxonomy suggestions are editable; (2) retention and privacy — payload snippets are redacted by default and require explicit reveal with audit logging; (3) complexity of runbook editing — keep inline lightweight editor with ability to export to Confluence/Drive for richer authoring.

Performance considerations: bulk payload diffing will run asynchronously with progressive reveal. Initial cluster summaries must load within 1s (target), detailed diffs may be streamed with a spinner and sampled preview.
Accessibility: keyboard-first navigation for triage steps, color choices compliant with WCAG for severity badges.
user_flows: Open Alerts -> Select failure cluster -> Orchestrator launches in split-panel (summary + sample payload list).
Review auto-suggested taxonomy nodes and accept/edit classifications.
Run sample payload replay (sandboxed) or view KV/prefix cache snapshot linked to the sample.
Generate payload diff between two selected samples; accept redaction presets and annotate differences.
Apply recommended remediation steps (one-click create runbook draft + add to rollout canary policy) or export to Confluence.
Resolve cluster and attach runbook to incident timeline for oncall postmortem.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Designer-approved mockups for cluster summary, payload list, diff surface, and runbook editor are linked and annotated.
AC-2: Prototype demonstrates taxonomy suggestion flow (accept/edit) and shows audit prompt for payload reveal.
AC-3: Product accepts the runbook export format (Confluence/Markdown) in a sample integration test with PM-supplied Confluence space.
AC-4: Engineering confirms feasibility of async payload diffing and streaming previews; acceptable performance envelope documented.
AC-5: Security signoff on payload redaction defaults and audit trail requirement (see links).
review_feedback: Evan Chen (Eng): prefer initial MVP to hide automated repair suggestions behind a feature flag until we validate false positive rate.
Priya Narang (PM): emphasize runbook-to-rollout handoff. Add a CTA to create a canary policy draft from the runbook steps.
Sana Mahmood (SRE): request explicit linkage to historical autoscaler incidents when recommending scaling-based remediation.
Design review (11/18): tweak severity color scale and make sample payload pagination persistent across sessions.
decisions: D-1: Hybrid taxonomy — suggest node but require explicit accept to commit classification to incident metadata.
D-2: Payloads are redacted by default; reveal requires owner permission and is recorded in audit logs (reduces PII risk).
D-3: Runbook editor will be a lightweight markdown area with structured steps and a 'Promote to Rollout' button that creates a canary template (backend work tracked separately).
D-4: MVP excludes automated remediation execution; only scaffold recipes and manual 'apply' actions are supported behind a beta flag.
next_steps: Finalize accessibility pass and annotate Figma with keyboard states (owner: Marco).
Eng spike to prototype async payload diffing and publish perf numbers (owner: Evan).
Add feature flag gating and create rollout proposal for Beta customers (owner: Priya).
Schedule security review for payload reveal flow and KMS audit hooks (owner: Ravi Kaur).
